hypothesis: Globally unique short content-ID prefixes reduce navigation-hint overhead without changing ranking; extra budget may increase file coverage.

policy_fixed_before_run.ranking: Existing BM25 scores, parameters, tokenization, and tie order are unchanged
policy_fixed_before_run.file_selection: Best-scoring chunk per file, in BM25 order
policy_fixed_before_run.preview: Line in the anchor chunk with most distinct query terms; source-order ties; trim whitespace; first 160 Unicode characters
policy_fixed_before_run.handles: Shortest globally unique SHA-256 prefix of at least 12 hex characters, extending on collision; full IDs remain accepted by expand. Text and JSON deliver the same short handle.
policy_fixed_before_run.order: Rotate tool order each repetition; execute sequentially

judgments: The same 30 authored requests are now development diagnostics, not held-out validation. This experiment changes only handle delivery/resolution, with no ranking or query-specific tuning.
primary_shared_metric: Code-file hint recall; hints do not count as delivered full source evidence
secondary_metrics: Code-file recall among first 5 and 10 delivered unique file hints
Actual delivered text tokens including IDs and previews
primary_efficiency_metric: Delivered retrieval-text tokens, including handles; never total agent usage
